title: Budget making in Porto Alegre
body: Porto Alegre, a city in Brazil with nearly 13 lakh people, set up a parallel organisation that works alongside its elected municipal council. The city is divided into sectors, similar to wards, and each sector holds a meeting, much like a gram sabha, where anyone living in that area can take part. Other meetings discuss issues that affect the whole city, and any citizen may join them. The city budget is discussed at these meetings, and the proposals are then sent to the municipality, which takes the final decision. About 20,000 people take part in this exercise every year. As a result, money is no longer spent only on colonies where rich people live: buses now run to poor colonies, and builders cannot evict slum-dwellers without resettling them. A similar experiment has taken place in some areas of Kerala, where ordinary people helped prepare development plans for their locality.
